mauritania.title: Flag of the Islamic Republic of Mauritania

colors.note: Field colour; represents Islam and the hope of a bright future.
Crescent and star; the crescent symbolises Islam and the star unity among the people.
Top and bottom stripes, added in 2017; represent the blood shed by defenders of the nation.

desc:
- A green field with a gold crescent (horns upward) and five-pointed star, bordered by red stripes at the top and bottom
- The green and gold design dates to independence in 1959
- The red stripes were added on 15 August 2017 following a constitutional referendum, honouring those who died defending Mauritania
- The crescent and star are pan-Islamic symbols; the crescent's upward-facing horns are a distinctive feature
- **Construction:** the green field occupies the central portion, with red stripes at top and bottom each 1/5 of the flag height
- The crescent is centred, opening upward, with the star above it
- Ratio 2:3
trivia:
- The green represents Islam; the red represents bloodshed for independence; white represents purity
- The star and crescent represent Islam and the nation's faith
- Mauritania's flag was adopted in 1959 and includes Islamic symbols in a Pan-African design

mauritania-1959.title: Former flag of Mauritania (1959–2017)

colors.note: Islam and the land of Mauritania.

desc:
- The original flag of Mauritania (1959–2017) was a green field with a gold crescent and star — without the red top and bottom stripes that were added in 2017
- This design was adopted upon independence from France on 28 November 1960 and remained unchanged for nearly six decades until a constitutional referendum on 5 August 2017 added the red stripes
- **Construction:** a green field with a gold crescent (horns upward) and five-pointed star centred. Ratio 2:3
trivia:
- Mauritania's original flag from 1959 upon independence from France
- Represented the nation's Islamic identity and Arab heritage
- Evolved with the addition of the Shahada inscription later
